mechanism.base: Old texts have it that metal keeps to the stone and is born where the ground stays damp. Ore does not form in the open. It waits under the hill, pressed by rock and fed by slow water, for longer than anything struck from it lasts. Earth gives the blade its substance first and its patience second, and a blade that forgets the ground it came from loses the second gift first.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: With too little Earth, the edge stands on thin ground and every judgment is struck before it has settled. Let one hard question sit overnight before you answer it.
mechanism.friction_turn: With too much Earth, the ore sits in the ground long after it is ready and no edge gets struck from it. Make one thing and let it leave the house.

catalyst.clause: the edge stands on thin ground and every judgment is struck before it has settled
catalyst.remedy: Let one hard question sit overnight before you answer it.

friction.clause: the ore sits in the ground long after it is ready and no edge gets struck from it
friction.remedy: Make one thing and let it leave the house.

wide.clause: There is no shortage of Earth in you, the slow ground the metal grows from.
wide.remedy: Use it. Settle one question you already know enough about.

missing.clause: Nothing feeds the metal here, so each judgment comes out with no time in the ground behind it.
missing.remedy: Borrow it from someone older, one slow conversation at a time.

spared.clause: There is no Earth here to pile on the metal, and the metal is lighter for it.
spared.remedy: Leave it be. Keep deciding at your own speed.

thin.clause: Only a little Earth sits on the metal, enough to steady it and not enough to slow it.
thin.remedy: Keep it that small. Study only what you will use.

excess.clause: Earth piles past what the metal uses, so the edge stalls where it lies and nothing gets struck.
excess.remedy: Put one thing out this month, rough as it is.

function.definition_catalyst: Earth is your Mind, and as a catalyst, it is the slow intake you run on. Because you carry less Earth than you use, you go short on private study and on a steady home. You want to be sure rather than fast, so you give a question one night before your judgment holds.
function.definition_friction: Earth is your Mind, and as a friction, it is intake with nowhere to go. You hold more Earth than you spend, so you keep learning ahead of deciding and sheltering ahead of letting go. Since preparing is where you feel most at ease, you keep the finished thing waiting past its time.
function.advise_catalyst: Your judgment is only as good as the time you let it take in. Read one book slowly instead of five fast. Ask the oldest person you trust how they would do it, and hear them out to the end. Keep one evening a week with no one in it. Sleep on anything that costs money.
function.advise_friction: Getting ready is your most comfortable way of not starting. Decide one thing you have read enough about. Send the rough version to someone before the clean one exists. Seek Wood, the Action energy. Wood grows from the ground that fed it, a thing built, a start made before the reading is done. Let it spend what Earth stores.

candidates.cta_verdict: You would rather understand a thing than be quick about it, so you keep only the answers you gave time to.

mechanism.base: Metal is born of earth, the old texts say: it lies in the mountain, gathered in stone, grown by slow pressure and the moisture of deep ground. Nothing hurries it. The mountain holds the ore for ages before any edge is struck from it, and every blade remembers the patience of the rock that made it.
mechanism.catalyst_turn: Run thin, the mountain goes hungry: a keen edge with nothing behind it, sharpness spent faster than it forms. Your chart asks you to feed the ground. Rest and study are smelting, not stalling.
mechanism.friction_turn: Run heavy, the shelter closes over the blade: so much preparation that the edge never leaves the mine. Comfort begins to bury what it formed. Dig out and cut something real.

catalyst.clause: The mountain goes hungry: a keen edge with nothing behind it, sharpness spent faster than it forms.
catalyst.remedy: Rest and study are smelting, not stalling.

friction.clause: The shelter closes over the blade: so much preparation that the edge never leaves the mine.
friction.remedy: Dig out and cut something real.

wide.clause: You are well supplied with Earth, the ground the ore grows in.
wide.remedy: Use what the ground gave you. Cut something.

missing.clause: No ground under the edge: judgment made on the spot, nothing settled in first.
missing.remedy: Borrow ground: a mentor, a book, one slow evening.

spared.clause: Earth runs absent, and the edge is lighter for it: nothing to bury it, nothing to shelter in.
spared.remedy: Keep it that way. Decide, then rest.

thin.clause: Earth runs thin and unwanted: a little shelter, easily left.
thin.remedy: Leave it as it is, small.

excess.clause: Too much earth clogs the metal: fed past use, the edge stalls, brooding where it should cut.
excess.remedy: Dig out. Less study, one real cut.

function.definition_catalyst: Earth is your Mind, and as a catalyst, it is a slow, deep intake that turns experience into ground you can stand on. Books, mentors, quiet corners, long walks after hard conversations: whatever feeds it comes back later as judgment.
function.definition_friction: Earth is your Mind, and as a friction, it is intake with no off switch. Study, comfort, preparation, shelter: everything that goes in counts as progress, so nothing ever has to come out. Learning becomes the most respectable way to stand still.
function.advise_catalyst: Deep minds underrate their own output, so build the habit of releasing some. Once a month, teach one thing you learned to one person, because explaining it is how you find out it is really yours. Keep one notebook instead of six. And say your slow answer out loud before someone faster says a worse one.
function.advise_friction: At some point more learning is just fear with a reading list. Trade study for evidence: for every hour that goes in, one small thing comes out where someone can see it. Give each research topic a decision date. Finish one old course before any new one gets your money.

$original.cta_verdict: Your mind takes things in slowly and keeps them forever, and your best judgments are the ones you let sit overnight.
